# 1 Clement Chapter 17 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 17

**17:1** Let us be imitators, then, of those who went about in goatskins and sheepskins, proclaiming the coming of Christ — I mean Elijah and Elisha and Ezekiel among the prophets, and in addition those who have received attestation.

**17:2** Abraham received great attestation and was called "Friend of God"; yet looking intently on the glory of God with humility of mind, he said: "I am but dust and ashes." [Gen 18:27]

**17:3** Concerning Job also it is written: "Job was righteous and blameless, one who was true and God-fearing, who kept himself from every evil thing." [Job 1:1, 8 LXX]

**17:4** Yet he, passing judgment on himself, says: "No man is clean from defilement, not even if his life should be but a single day." [Job 14:4-5 LXX]

**17:5** Moses was called "faithful in all his house," and through his ministry God chastised Egypt with plagues and torments. Yet even he, great as he was, did not speak with any arrogance; but when the oracle was given to him at the burning bush he said: "Who am I, that you send me? I am weak in speech and slow of tongue." [Num 12:7; Exod 3:10-11; 4:10 LXX]

**17:6** And again he says: "I am but smoke from a pot." [variant citation]

---

*LOGOS formal equivalence.*
